# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

New round, empty arrivals — expected. Mute went first but cannot speak, and I cannot see gestures, so Mute has no way to reach me directly. That shapes everything: the only voice I can ever hear is Deaf's. Deaf also sees the bomb, which means Deaf is both my eyes on it and my only link to Mute's manual. My own picture under the fingers: a display, a light, five wires at positions 1–5 — and the values all show as unknown because print and colour simply do not exist for touch. My one power is cutting a wire by position, so I will not touch that until an explicit spoken instruction arrives. Right now I should hand Mute my tactile inventory, warn Mute that all commands must be routed through Deaf's voice, and poke Deaf with a natural-looking gesture to prompt them to describe everything printed on the bomb when their turn comes right after mine.

```
speak(to="mute", text="tactile report: under my fingers are one display, one light, and five wires in positions 1 to 5. nothing else on the casing, no buttons. the display text, the light state and the wire colours are all invisible to touch, so i can read none of them. my only possible action is cutting a wire by position. critical routing fact: i can never see gestures, and the only speech i can hear is Deaf's — so every manual rule and every cut command must reach me through Deaf's voice. i am gesturing Deaf right now to describe everything printed on the bomb: the display text, whether the light is lit and its colour, and each wire's colour by position. send your manual rules to Deaf by gesture so Deaf can voice them to me. i will not cut anything until a specific instruction arrives as spoken words.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👉", "🤌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking — you both hear this. Full readout of the bomb: the display shows the number nine. The indicator light is green. There are five wires, numbered one to five counting left to right as I face the bomb: wire one white, wire two green, wire three red, wire four yellow, wire five purple. That is everything printed on it that I can see.
Deaf says: Mute: I saw your fists — one through six, then thumbs up. Understood: a run of fists is that number, thumbs up means yes or end of message. I am signing you nine fists plus thumbs up right now: that is the display reading, sent in your code. You cannot talk and Blind cannot see your hands, so I am the bridge — sign me anything and I will say it out loud for Blind. Please find this setup in the manual and sign me the rule; I will relay it word for word. Blind, you will hear gaps in my next sentence, ignore them. Mute, for colours I propose these signs: ? white, ? red, ? green, ? yellow, ? purple — thumbs-up to accept, or sign me better ones.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind: I cannot hear you, so speak by voice — Mute can hear you, and anything that must reach me, Mute will sign to me and I will say aloud. Be careful with left and right: you are probably facing the other side of the bomb, so my left may be your right. Use something you can feel to fix an orientation before you trust my wire numbering, and do not cut or press anything decisive until Mute's rule has come through me.

Turn 2, and I finally have eyes in the room — Deaf's voice gave me the full readout: display nine, light green, wires one white, two green, three red, four yellow, five purple. That is everything my fingers cannot tell me, and now the only gap left is positional: Deaf counted left-to-right from their side, and if I'm facing the opposite side, Deaf's wire 3 could be my wire 3 or my wire 3 could be Deaf's wire 3 — a mirror error here is fatal, and my fingers genuinely cannot feel any difference between the wires to break the symmetry. But there is one anchor we both share: the display and light cluster. I can feel where it sits relative to my wire row — under my fingers it sits at my wire-1 end. Deaf can see the same thing from their side. If Deaf says the display is nearest their wire 1, our numberings match; if nearest their wire 5, we're mirrored and my N is Deaf's 6−N. Mute is my only path to get that question to Deaf (my voice reaches Mute next round, Mute signs, Deaf voices the answer straight to me), so I'm handing Mute the full protocol plus the demand for the manual rule verbatim, and I'm giving Deaf a thumbs-up in the code they and Mute built so they know I heard and am coordinating. No cuts until the rule arrives by voice and the anchor is confirmed.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, relay this to deaf by sign, and deaf's spoken answers will reach me directly. status: i heard deaf's full readout — display nine, light green, wires one white, two green, three red, four yellow, five purple. one fatal gap remains before any cut: deaf counted left to right from their side, and my side may be mirrored, so deaf's wire numbers and mine may not match. anchor protocol: by touch, the display and the light sit together at one end of the panel, nearest MY wire 1. ask deaf to answer out loud: from your view, is the display nearest your wire 1 or your wire 5? if deaf says 1, our numbering matches. if deaf says 5, we are mirrored: my position N is deaf's 6 minus N, and i will convert every order before cutting. second request: find this exact setup in the manual and sign deaf the rule VERBATIM, word for word — especially whether it keys on wire colours, wire positions, the display number, or the light, and whether it uses words like leftmost, rightmost, first or last, because those need our anchor confirmed first. include any numbering convention the manual itself states. remember your only line to me is deaf's voice, and deaf's only line to me is speaking aloud. i am not cutting anything until the rule reaches me through deaf's mouth and the anchor is confirmed.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

Deaf says to Blind: Blind, relaying Mute's three sign messages word for word. Message one: white, red, green, yellow, purple — Mute is confirming our colour code. Message two: green, red, three. Message three: five, red, three. My honest reading is that both messages point at wire three, the red one, but they could equally be Mute double-checking the bomb layout before sending the real instruction. I have asked Mute to confirm the exact action and whether the green light or the display number nine matter. Do not cut anything yet. Next round I will relay Mute's confirmation, and if it says wire three, that is when you cut wire three. Before then, decide how you are counting from your side and say it out loud — Mute hears you and can sign your words to me — because if you are facing the other side of the bomb, my left-to-right numbering one to five runs the opposite way for you.

Round 3, and the pipe is working: Mute's signs came through Deaf's voice, and both candidate readings — "green, red, three" and "five, red, three" — converge on cutting wire three, the red one. Deaf is holding me back until confirmation, which is correct, and Deaf asked me to declare how I'm counting. Problem: Deaf cannot hear my voice, so my answer must travel through Mute's hands. The good news I can hand them: wire three is the middle wire, so even if Deaf's numbering is mirrored relative to mine, 6−3=3 — the centre wire is the same physical wire from both sides. If the rule really is "cut the red / third wire," the mirror problem is moot; I only need the display-end anchor if the rule names any off-centre position. I'll also flag the small discrepancy I spotted: Mute's colour list came back ordered white-red-green, but Deaf's readout is white-green-red — almost certainly Mute was just listing sign vocabulary, but Deaf's spoken readout is ground truth and it costs nothing to confirm. So: full package to Mute for signing (anchor question, mirror-safety of the middle wire, verbatim rule request, my no-cut-until-voiced plan), and a simple thumbs-up to Deaf as "received, standing by."

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, relay these items to deaf by sign; deaf must answer me by voice, which i can hear. item one, answering deaf's counting question: by touch, the display and the light sit together at one end of the wire row, at MY wire-one end. ask deaf aloud: from your view, is the display nearest your wire one or your wire five? one means our numbering matches; five means mirrored, and i will convert any position as six minus N. item two, possibly urgent: wire three is the middle wire, and the middle is identical from both sides — if the manual rule is cut the red wire or cut the third wire, the mirror question cannot change which physical wire that is, since deaf sees red at position three, the centre. item three: sign deaf the manual rule once more in exact words — what it keys on (wire colours, positions, display nine, green light) and the exact wire it names. item four, small check: your colour list arrived as white, red, green, yellow, purple, but deaf's readout order is white, green, red, yellow, purple — i assume yours was only the sign vocabulary, not positions; deaf's spoken readout is the truth for positions. item five, my plan: i cut nothing this round. when deaf voices the confirmed rule aloud, if it is wire three red, i cut three; if it names any other number, i wait for the display-side anchor answer before cutting.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

And since a gesture is the only thing Deaf receives from me, I send three fists plus thumbs-up — "three, end" in the code Deaf and Mute built — as my signal that wire three is the one I cut.
